svg.text: Count pairs divisible by K — two ways to use remainders A = [2,2,1,7,5,3], K = 4
Two values pair up when their remainders add to K: remainder r pairs with remainder (K−r).
Approach 1 — bucket all remainders first, then pair the buckets

g.text: remainder 0 alone pairs with itself: count[0] = 0 → 0 pairs
K is even (4), so remainder K/2=2 also pairs with itself:
remaining remainders 1 .. K/2−1 pair with K−r:
r=1 pairs with r=3: count[1]×count[3] = 2×2 = 4 pairs

svg.text: This matches the expected output of 5 for this example.
Approach 2 — single pass, look up (K − rem) in the map built SO FAR
This avoids double counting because at each step we only look at elements seen BEFORE it.

g.text: v=2 rem=2 look for (4-2=2) in map={} not found map={2:1} cnt=0
v=2 rem=2 look for (4-2=2) in map={2:1} FOUND (1) cnt+=1 map={2:2} cnt=1
v=1 rem=1 look for (4-1=3) in map={2:2} not found map={2:2,1:1} cnt=1
v=7 rem=3 look for (4-3=1) in map={2:2,1:1} FOUND (1) cnt+=1 map={2:2,1:1,3:1} cnt=2
v=5 rem=1 look for (4-1=3) in map={...,3:1} FOUND (1) cnt+=1 map={2:2,1:2,3:1} cnt=3
v=3 rem=3 look for (4-3=1) in map={...,1:2} FOUND (2) cnt+=2 map={2:2,1:2,3:2} cnt=5

svg.text: Final answer: cnt = 5 — same result, one single pass, no separate remainder==0 loop needed.
when rem == 0, pair it with the rem == 0 entries already stored (not with K − 0 = K, which is out of the 0..K−1 remainder range).
